mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 3.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 3-month moving averages signals strengthening labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 3-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of aggressive monetary easing.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change < -1% for 4 consecutive months and FEDFUNDS not < 1%
regime_hint: persistent income contraction outside monetary easing
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS falls by more than 1% year-over-year for four consecutive months and FEDFUNDS is not in a clear easing cycle.
